AA Prototype · Requirements catch-up

The catch-up: from the RFP to the catalogue

The prototype was built in July against the original RFP, in fourteen phases. The requirements catalogue has since become the source of truth and moved a long way: Bookings instead of Cards, Slots and Draft Lists, one Contract per Procedure locked at authorise, admin-decided hospital matching, an internal ledger with Xero as its mirror. This plan closes every verified gap in 43 further phases, numbered 14 to 44, each one focused session (at most two) with one coherent deliverable, and every automatic or external event given a demo button on the screen where it matters.

What changed since the prototype

The prototype is still the July RFP model. The EP-01 canvas, billing-run isolation, audit, NHI validation, per-anaesthetist unit value, GST-exclusive maths and the 15a warning registry match the catalogue. Almost everything else sits one design generation behind. Across the ~190 graded items there are only a handful of Matches (US-05.2.1, 05.2.6, 05.2.7, 05.3.5, 05.4.2, US-11.1.1, FT-03.2) and a large share of Contradicts: not missing features but the old design standing where a new one is required. The gap is structural, not cosmetic. Five foundations (Slot/Draft List, Contract/Procedure model, ledger payable, prepayment model, intake matching) must be rebuilt before most screens can be touched. Verified counts: 46 data-model deltas (DM-13 to DM-38, none refuted) and 34 reverse-check findings (RV-nn). Rough total: well over 40 XL/L blocks, but they collapse into about 8 shared builds (below). Do not sum the item sizes: many items share one build.

The themes below are the gap analysis's own grouping. Each lists the phases that carry its items. Full reasoning: GAP-ANALYSIS.md.

  1. Contract decides price and payer

    Route and Type 1/2/3 replaced by one Contract per Procedure with holder pays-AA rule, single No contract (RVG), dated versions, lines, AA code, snapshot at AUTHORISED. XL, foundation for pricing/billing/prepayment.

    20 items · built in phases 18, 20, 19a, 21, 25

  2. Procedure master and capture rework

    Procedure master, RVG group hierarchy, two-tab picker, modifier records with explanations, ASA as ordinary modifier, locked age/included modifiers, real RVG values, rate x time removed, source wording kept. XL, shared BtmCaptureBlock lands on all three apps.

    22 items · built in phases 19, 19b, 20, 39b, 20a, 19a, 24

  3. Pricing precedence and adjustment gatingL

    Anaesthetist adjustment gated to No contract and first-party Contracts, separate office override, independent fixed rate and discount, no-charge invoice, modifier split above four units. L.

    14 items · built in phases 23, 24, 19a

  4. Slot, Draft List and List lifecycleXL

    Optional anaesthetist on List, DRAFT/ACTIVE rename, Draft List admin page and creation paths, statuses as master data, return-or-assign on mark-unavailable, anaesthetist moves own List, tiers and private pairings. XL, structural first.

    30 items · built in phases 17, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 32a, 15b

  5. Hospital intake via matching screen

    Staged import rows, per-row admin decision, field-difference approval, unmatched queue; nothing auto-applies. HL7/FHIR/dead-letter tooling is Future and should be demoted. L shared build.

    15 items · built in phases 33, 34, 35, 20a

  6. Prepayment replacedXL

    Profile prepaid set, fixed price from first-party Contract, auto-draft with admin approval and letter, trust account held until procedure done, refund on cancel, no deposit or automatic settlement. XL; payable currently released before procedure.

    23 items · built in phases 26, 27, 41

  7. Ledger payable, credit notes, additional invoices, payment cycle

    Promote payable into ledger, remove 5% fee netting, credit-and-rebill, additional invoices and events, weekly payment cycle and approval, cash-basis GST. XL combined; do fee un-netting once.

    22 items · built in phases 39, 38b, 22, 39a, 16, 36, 38

  8. Admin oversight: warnings, notifications, NHI, balances

    Admin to-do dashboard on the existing warning registry with new rules, notification pool, NHI add/block/problem list, ledger positions without ageing, review warnings. M to L.

    21 items · built in phases 15a, 21, 32, 36, 38, 40, 42

  9. Past work and anaesthetist app polish

    Archive/search and scroll-back for billed Lists, prepaid amount display, source/Contract stack on booking screens. M.

    8 items · built in phases 38a, 27, 20a, 20, 21

  10. Remove or hide superseded features

    Copy a Booking, photo capture, Surgeon PDF tab, automated hospital changes, dashboard Productivity and Leave, ACC review flag; badge or hide Future-scope tooling.

    10 items · built in phases 15, 18, 33, 34, 35, 38, 39, 15b, 44

How this works

  1. Get the owner decisions first. D1 to D11 (the table at the top of ROADMAP.md) each gate one phase. A phase whose answer has not come in builds the stated default and labels it provisional.
  2. Pick the next phase from the table below, respecting the order in "Sequencing and rules". The Contracts track (17 to 25) and the Schedule track (28 to 32) each run strictly in order.
  3. Open a fresh Claude Code session and paste that phase's kick-off prompt. The agent reads the roadmap, its phase doc, the gap detail for its items, the prototype maps and PROGRESS.md before touching anything.
  4. Drift check first. The catalogue keeps moving. Each session diffs its items against 60e2d1e, reports what changed, and adapts the plan before building.
  5. The agent plans and builds straight on. It turns the phase doc into work-sized steps and starts building without waiting for approval, so phases can run back to back (ROADMAP.md "Owner review: agents test themselves").
  6. Every phase ends the same way: npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run and (for UI work) npm run shots green; the checklist run and reported item by item; the adversarial review-and-fix pass (PROGRESS convention 18); the demo guide patched for any beat it broke; the catalogue screenshots brought in step with the app (the phase's capture recipes created or updated, then a full npm run capture in requirements-board/ with no failed recipe and npm run verify:board green, PROGRESS convention 19); a PROGRESS.md entry. Agents never commit.
  7. When the catalogue changes, follow README.md: re-grade the changed items, merge them into gaps.json, update the affected phase docs, and re-render this page with node docs/prototype-build/catch-up/tools/build-index.mjs.

Demo buttons live on their screens. Anything that cannot be shown through normal use (scheduled jobs, backend events, external systems) gets a trigger in the harness bar's "Demo actions" menu, listed only on the screen where it matters. The installed PWA has no harness bar, so it gets the same list as a badged demo-actions sheet, plus office stand-ins for beats that wait on the office. Phase 14 builds the mechanism; every later phase registers into it.

The checklists are the contract. Each phase ends with a short manual test checklist. The agent runs it itself in the running app and reports each item with evidence; nothing is handed to the owner per phase. Each PROGRESS entry ends with a "For the owner's review" list, and Phase 44 gathers them into one list for a single review once every catch-up phase is done.

Sequencing and rules

Owner decisions (table at the top of ROADMAP.md). D1 to D8 and D10 were answered on 2026-10-01 and D12 to D25 on 2026-10-02; the 2026-10-08 update (catalogue 60e2d1e) re-read every row. Pricing model in one place. The draft technical design v4 (AR-29 regions data-model, contract-holder-fields, contract-fields, contract-line-fields, booking-procedure-fields, contract-behaviour, contract-selection, resolver-layers, null-handling, price-validation, price-precedence, pricing-snapshot, billable-party, prepayment, contract-versions, data-loading) and its ERD (AR-30: rvg-group, procedure, contract-line, contract, contract-holder, booking-procedure) are the reference shape for RVG groups, procedures, contract holders, Contracts, Contract lines and booking procedures, but they are a draft that a v5 may change before or during the build. Every phase that builds these structures (18, 19, 19a, 19b, 20, 20a, 21, 23, 24, 25, 27) keeps the structures, the resolver and the price precedence in one place in aa-prototype/src/domain/billing (plus the seed), behind types the UI reads, so a later design change stays a contained edit; each says so in its Goal or Work items and links AR-28 (the plain-language guide, true as written), AR-29 and AR-30 at the regions it builds (21 adds AR-30#contract-holder and #booking-procedure; 24 AR-29#booking-procedure-fields and AR-30#booking-procedure; 25 AR-28#keeping-prices-up-to-date and AR-30#booking-procedure and #contract; 19b AR-29#booking-procedure-fields and AR-30#booking-procedure). AR-35 declares no regions: 20a links AR-35 and cites its note's 'Illustrative source wording' heading by name, never an invented anchor, and the plan update does not edit the artifact. 43's generator builds through the same module, never a second copy of the shapes. Modifiers are seeded from NZSA RVG 2021 modifiers.md and NZSA RVG 2021 included modifiers.csv (AR-34), never re-transcribed from the RVG. Items that Match only because of the old model (US-05.2.6's fixed rate through Type 2's agreedUnitRate, FT-03.2's primary Procedure, US-05.2.1, US-05.2.7, US-05.3.5, US-05.4.2, FT-08.2's grouping, FT-05.5's ACC as an ordinary holder, US-09.1.3's prepayment Xero pair) are carried across without regression, with parity tests, by 18, 19a, 20, 21, 23, 24 and 27.

Vocabulary. Booking, not Card; move or reassign, never swap; never 'timesheet'. Per OQ-64, 'slot' never reaches app copy (say session, AM or PM); Slot stays a code and planning word. A List's states are DRAFT (a Draft List, no anaesthetist), ACTIVE, SUBMITTED and AUTHORISED; never 'DRAFT' for an assigned List after 15b, and no 'Open' label for one. 'Draft List' is kept. 'Not preferred' and 'Preferred', never 'blacklist' or 'whitelist', in app copy. The catalogue's Procedure is the design's booking procedure; 'procedure' alone means a procedure-list entry. 'Event' is the one name for everything recorded against a Procedure after setup; keep its user-facing label in one place (38b), because Greg was unconvinced by it. The prepaid amount is never called an estimate or a deposit.

BCTI granularity (provisional, one place). The catalogue says both 'one BCTI per procedure' (US-09.1.4 note, OQ-29, note #41) and 'the same value as its receivable' (OQ-42), and a receivable can hold several Procedures, so both cannot hold (DM-22 says so). The plan builds one BCTI, the ACCPAY, per receivable invoice, the same value: the transcript's 'per transaction' (B L71-81), which US-10.2.1's release needs. 16 counts BCTIs for the fee run through one pure, tested function, each once against the anaesthetist who did it and, per Greg's 2026-10-02 view for the accountant, only once paid, both switchable there; 22 (a split gives two invoices, so two BCTIs), 36 (the ledger's payable legs, with a parity test), 38b (additional invoices), 39 (re-issued invoices; whether a credit note or negative invoice counts is OQ-60), 39b (event invoices) and 43 (generated history) feed it and keep it the only count. 'One per procedure' stays an open point to raise with AA's accountant beside OQ-29 and OQ-60; if it flips, the count function, the $700 seed and the S3 and S4 figures are re-baselined in one place.

Demo triggers. 14 re-homed every existing Control Panel trigger onto its screen and added useDemoTriggerContext for state outside the URL; later phases register or re-point entries, never add to the Control Panel page, which is the index (scenario jumps, clock, reset). Entries declare routes, surfaces (bar, PWA, both), run(api, ctx) on the entity in the URL or the published context, and a disabled state; bodies live in src/shared or src/store for pwaPurity. Product actions (Split, Approve and send, Create additional invoice, Credit note, Draft update email, Import hospital bookings) stay in the product UI. 15a's 'Raise sample warnings' is shared: each phase that adds a warning rule adds its sample. PWA parity: every beat whose mobile side waits on the office, a colleague or a backend event gets a PWA-only stand-in on that mobile screen (listed per phase, including 21's Contract-change approval, 27's approve and send, 31's Draft List assignment, 32's and 32a's colleague moves, 38b's and 39b's office reviews, 40's NHI attach and 43a's Sign out); 'Play the office' defaults OFF with a badge; 44 audits parity beat by beat.

Catalogue screenshots. Every phase ends with the standing capture step (ROADMAP.md 'Catalogue screenshots': recipes for covered and broken items, a full npm run capture with no failed recipe, npm run verify:board). Stale captions that describe old behaviour are replaced by the phase that rebuilds the screen, and its 'Catalogue screenshots' rows say what the new shot must show: US-04.3.3 (20: No contract (RVG) first), US-03.3.4 (19b: optional itemised modifiers with the explanation asked on claiming, locked age and P1), US-06.2.2 and US-06.3.1 (27: the fixed price from the first-party Contract, generated with its draft Xero pair), US-08.2.2 (27: the deduction leaving nothing to bill), US-06.4.1 (41: nothing automatic, the by-hand routes), US-04.2.2 (24: line terms and precedence), the US-05.1.x captions (19, 19a, 19b), US-03.1.2 (20a: the stack), US-11.2.x (21: the payer on the Booking) and US-07.4.1 (38a: the main view and the archive); 40a's US-14.4.1 shots are re-taken on an ACTIVE List. The plan update itself never touches recipes or images.

Every phase opens with a drift check against 60e2d1e (15a against 3d3a18c, read with its dated section) and closes with npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run, and npm run shots (Playwright) for any phase touching UI, all green; the adversarial review pass (PROGRESS convention 18); the catalogue screenshot step; PERSIST_VERSION bumped on seed changes; Decisions-log entries where a ruling is superseded (the route model, 5% fee netting, Copy as an additional procedure and then Phase 15's skeleton Copy, binding convention 6's DRAFT for an assigned List, absorbed P1 modifiers, the 2026-07-22 ASA seeding values, the protected default Type 1 per hospital and insurer, the Method 3 hourly rate line, the guardian override record, the 2026-09-28 fee hidden from the anaesthetist where the catalogue now shows a price, the addendum Card, the prepayment completion gate, the prepayment estimate and deposit, the overpaid prepayment's negativeTotal failure, the silent BTM fallback, availability reconciliation's conflict flag, office write-through per tap, the cover-request flow, hospital auto-apply, Surgeon PDFs kept in scope by Phase 14); a PROGRESS entry with its 'For the owner's review' list. Agents test themselves: no plan-approval stop, the agent runs the manual test checklist in the running app, open questions become built defaults logged for the owner, and the owner reviews once after 44.

Screen-contextual demo triggers

Foundations Start here 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 1 item covered

Build one shared, pure trigger registry in src/shared/demoTriggers (its own index, modelled on demoClockShortcuts, not re-exported from the shared component barrel), plus a small useDemoTriggerContext hook for screen state the URL cannot carry, such as the Admin Integrations tab and the simulator's selected message. Each entry declares its route patterns, where it shows (harness bar, PWA sheet or both), a run(api, ctx) that acts on the entity in the URL or on the published state, a disabled reason, and an index link with an optional hint. The harness bar gets one 'Demo actions' pill that lists only the current screen's triggers and is hidden when there are none. The PWA gets the same list as a badged bottom sheet. Every Control Panel trigger moves to its own screen, except 'Run payables', whose home is the Billing monitor's existing product button. The Control Panel becomes the index, keeping scenario jumps, clock and reset. FT-13.5 gets a 'Simulate sign-in attempts' trigger on Admin Audit that writes five audit rows. 'Play the office' is off by default, badged when on, and replaced in the story by a per-List 'Office authorises this List'. The HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges, and S1 gets a caveat.

FT-13.5board
Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Audit: 'Simulate sign-in attempts' (an Admin sign-in with MFA, a failed attempt, an anaesthetist self-service password reset)
  • Admin Billing monitor: 'Trigger billing failure', 'Arm handoff failure', 'Run payables', 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed from the Control Panel)
  • Admin Review, on Dr Sharma's Tue 14 Jul List: 'Stage post-op scenario' (re-homed)
  • Admin Integrations, Surgeon PDFs tab (read through the context hook): 'Ingest PDF row' (re-homed)
  • Admin invoice document and Xero pair detail: 'Payment received (webhook)' Full or Half, and 'Replay last event', for the invoice in the URL (re-homed)
  • Xero sim: 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed)
  • Integrations simulator, Admin Integrations and mobile Lists: 'Fire hospital message' and 'Replay last (dedupe)', badged Future scope (re-homed; S1 fires it from the mobile screen)
  • PWA sheet, mobile List: 'Office authorises this List' (so 'Play the office' can default OFF, badged when on)
  • PWA sheet, mobile Balances: 'Payment received' Full or Half on an open invoice

Risks. pwaPurity.test forbids shell or demo imports in the PWA closure, so the registry, the context hook, trigger bodies and shared OFFICE and SOUTER actor constants live in src/shared or src/store. The 48px bar has no responsive handling: one menu pill, not many buttons. Office stand-ins declare the PWA surface only, because in the framed build the presenter plays the office in Admin. Playwright data-shot hooks (control-payment-webhook, control-scheduled-jobs, control-integration-message) move with their triggers, so the specs change here. Re-home first and re-green, then add the new pieces.

What to check when it's done
  • The harness bar shows no 'Demo actions' pill on the Admin Day view. On the Billing monitor it lists exactly four entries. Every Control Panel 'Open screen' link, with its hint where shown, lands on a screen whose menu contains that entry, and no trigger buttons remain on the Control Panel.
  • Each re-homed trigger behaves exactly as its Control Panel card did: same store calls, actors, guards and idempotency keys, and half-payment falls back to the full amount when half rounds to 0. 'Ingest PDF row' appears only on the Surgeon PDFs tab. Replay after a reset refuses cleanly.
  • Installed PWA with fresh or corrupt storage: 'Play the office' is OFF and a submitted List waits. The Demo chip on that List runs 'Office authorises this List', which authorises and bills it. Balances takes a chosen payment. pwaPurity.test stays green, with the bar menu forbidden.
  • 'Simulate sign-in attempts' adds five labelled audit rows through mutate() only: provisioning, Admin sign-in with MFA, failed sign-in, self-service reset and mobile social login. Future-scope badges show on the simulator and on the Messages and Feed config tabs. The S1 caveat is in place. build, build:pwa, vitest, shots and verify:board are all green, and the 4 specs, 18 recipes and ATLAS are updated.
Kick-off prompt - paste into a fresh Claude Code session 
Please run catch-up Phase 14 (Screen-contextual demo triggers) of the Anaesthesia Associates prototype.

Repo root: /Users/d.fraser/Local Dev/Anaesthesia Associates RFP (the folder name has spaces, so quote paths). The app is aa-prototype/; every path below is relative to the repo root. Follow CLAUDE.md. Do not commit or push.

Before doing anything else, read these in order:
1. docs/prototype-build/catch-up/ROADMAP.md - the sequencing rules and the "Demo triggers", "PWA parity" and "Demo guide" sections (this phase builds the mechanism every later phase registers into).
2. docs/prototype-build/catch-up/phases/phase-14-demo-trigger-registry.md - your detailed plan.
3. docs/prototype-build/catch-up/GAP-ANALYSIS.md - "Demo-trigger buttons", "Remove or rework" and "Demo impact (S1 to S5)"; then docs/prototype-build/catch-up/epics/EP-13.md (FT-13.5) and docs/prototype-build/catch-up/analysis/reverse-check.md (RV-05, RV-06, RV-22).
4. The catalogue items: "requirements-board/requirements/stories/FT-13.5.md", US-13.5.1.md and US-13.5.2.md in the same folder.
5. docs/prototype-build/catch-up/analysis/prototype-map-shell-demo-pwa.md (all of it: every Control Panel trigger, the PWA panel and office simulation, the extension points) and the Audit, Billing monitor, Invoices and Integrations sections of prototype-map-admin.md.
6. docs/design/Design Language.dc.html (tokens, badge tints, sheet-in motion) and docs/design/Mobile App.dc.html (the bottom-sheet pattern, and the header and dock positions the PWA chip must clear). The harness bar has no mockup: copy aa-prototype/src/shell/DemoClockMenu.tsx.

Then aa-prototype/README.md's Office simulation section and the "Demo control panel" section of requirements-board/capture/ATLAS.md.
8. requirements-board/capture/ATLAS.md (the recipe format, routes, ids and hooks the catalogue's screenshot recipes depend on) and the "Catalogue screenshots" rule in docs/prototype-build/catch-up/ROADMAP.md. This phase also runs the baseline sweep in the phase doc's Catalogue screenshots section.

Then do the drift check in the phase doc (git diff 501b0b8 for FT-13.5, its two stories, US-07.2.2, US-07.3.1 and FT-14.1 to 14.6), and report what changed. Enter plan mode: confirm the registry contract (types, surfaces, when, choices, disabledReason, indexPath, indexHint, memory, context keys), map each Control Panel handler to its registry entry (and say which one, "Run payables", is dropped because the Billing monitor's product button is its home), split the work into the two sessions the doc describes, and wait for my approval. Do not edit any file before I approve.

While working:

- Mock backend only. Every new write is an office-only store action through the audited mutate(), with before/after metas and timestamps from the demo clock. Components never own domain state.
- Determinism: add no surgeons and do not touch the canvas pick arrays (CES_SURGEONS, GENERAL_SURGEONS) or any generator input; prove the canvas is unchanged with a seed fingerprint test written before any seed edit. Seed timestamps are fixed strings. Bump PERSIST_VERSION by one. The within-tier shuffle uses mulberry32 from src/domain/rng.ts keyed on the List id plus a stored request counter (suggestionSeq in the shell slice, bumped each time an office candidate picker opens, zeroed by Reset): never Math.random, never the wall clock; the same key replays the same order.
- HPI CPN (OQ-52 answered): one required hpiId on the surgeon, labelled "HPI CPN" everywhere, the surgeon's unique index; stored trimmed and upper-cased, shape-checked (two digits, four letters) and refused when blank, malformed or already held by any surgeon or anaesthetist. No separate CPN field; the NZ registration number is "for information"; relabel the audit field hpiId from "HPI id" to "HPI CPN", and the Admin add and edit anaesthetist labels too (the anaesthetist's stays optional, "where available", but a typed one is normalised and must not clash with a surgeon's). Never present it as the patient NHI.
- Pairing preferences (OQ-43 answered, D44): one PairingPreference model with kind (NOT_PREFERRED or PREFERRED) and raisedBy (SURGEON or ANAESTHETIST), an optional reason, added and ended by the office (history kept, audited) from either the surgeon profile or the Admin anaesthetist record, and shown on both through one shared Admin PairingSection. Both sides of one pair may be active; a same-side duplicate, or a same-side entry of the other kind, is refused. Not preferred on either side wins over preferred.
- Priority tiers (US-01.3.6, D36): four tiers, Tier 1 highest, Tier 4 the default for any anaesthetist with no entry (so a new anaesthetist is Tier 4). Held in the office-only slice keyed by anaesthetist id, NOT on the Anaesthetist record (that record reaches the anaesthetist apps). Set on the Admin anaesthetist record page, with a mist line that the tier names are provisional while OQ-102 is open.
- Privacy is the point. Preferences and tiers live in a new officePrivate state slice; their actions and selectors are in src/store/officePrivate.ts, which is NOT re-exported from the src/store barrel; the reusable UI is Admin-only in src/apps/admin/components/pairing/. Add src/apps/officePrivacy.test.ts: an allowlist source scan (no mobile, web, pwa, shell, demo or non-audit shared file names the slice, the types or those modules), a PWA-closure check (never reaches store/officePrivate.ts or apps/admin), a history check (no pairing or tier audit entry renders in a history the anaesthetist apps open; filter through one OFFICE_PRIVATE_AUDIT_ACTIONS set if needed), and a vocabulary check (no "blacklist" or "whitelist" string in src outside comments). An anaesthetist actor's store writes never read, check or log preferences. The fake backend runs in the browser, so the seeded slice still ships in every build's in-memory store: the boundary is screens, selectors and the PWA closure; log that limit for the owner rather than contorting the seed.
- One rule, one place. All grouping, tier ordering, shuffling, filtering and warnings go through the pure src/domain/pairingPreferences.ts (groupSurgeonsForAnaesthetist, rankAnaesthetistCandidates, notPreferredWarning, pairingSentence), never inline in a sheet or a store action. Tiers order the candidates within each group (the assumed combination); preferred pairings are marked, not re-ordered.
- One name set, one place. Every user-facing kind and tier word builds from PAIRING_LABELS and TIER_LABELS ("Not preferred", "Preferred", Tier 1 to Tier 4), and every side sentence from pairingSentence. Never "blacklist" or "whitelist" in app copy. Audit codes are pairing.add, pairing.end, anaesthetist.tierSet and *.pairingAcknowledged.
- Not preferred warns the office and never blocks, on every office path that exists today (Edit list, phone advice booking, Permanent List sheet, Reassign list): the option sits in its own labelled group and stays selectable; choosing it shows a soft amber warning naming the pairing and the side before save; going ahead writes one *.pairingAcknowledged audit entry. It is an assignment-time check, not a Booking warning: register nothing in 15a's routine and post nothing to the to-do list or the notification pool. Nothing anaesthetist-facing is built (US-01.4.5: no warning on an own hand-on, Phases 32 and 32a).
- Room membership has one source, Surgeon.roomId. Surgeon groups are a new master beside organisations; leave the COS Contract and organisations alone for Phase 18.
- src/domain never imports from src/shared. Seed pairing ids use PP- (runtime PPN).
- Keep S2 intact. Seed the surgeon-side not-preferred Reid with Sharma ("Surgeon's preference"), the ended anaesthetist-side Hughes with Reid, the surgeon-side preferred Whitford with Sharma, and demo-plausible tiers (five directors in Tier 1, the rest spread with some left at the Tier 4 default). Re-check with the seed test before seeding; if the canvas has moved, pick another and re-point the shots. Beat 2's surgeon picker shows Reid apart without touching the scripted Hale path; Beat 3's reassign (Rutherford Wed 22 AM to Sharma) shows the tier order and Sharma's Preferred pill with no warning; keep the isScriptedS2Booking prefill working.
- Add no new "permanent list" wording; Phase 30 renames it. Never say "slot" in app copy (say session, AM or PM).
- No demo triggers in this phase (it is all normal Admin use; nothing is anaesthetist-facing, so no PWA stand-in). Add nothing to the Control Panel.
- Design: warning tint for the warning (never error red), neutral pills for tiers, a calm pill for Preferred, teal the only action colour, crimson never used. The profile and record are real desktop pages and the sheets use useSurface().Overlay. No en or em dashes in any app copy.
- Keep npm run build, npm run build:pwa and npx vitest run green as you go. Add Vitest tests for the domain helpers (both kinds, both sides, both together, tier order, shuffle replay and variation, filter, the side sentence, the HPI CPN normaliser and shape check), the store actions (refusals, duplicate HPI CPN, same-side duplicate and contradiction refused, other side accepted, audit, end keeps history, tier set and default, acknowledgement), the privacy test, and the seed invariants (unique HPI CPNs, rooms, references, the seeded pairings and tiers, S2 path clear, canvas unchanged).

The Split button sits on the Contract part of 20a's three-part stack on the mobile (framed and PWA), web and Admin Booking screens, and the Contract part then reads "Split: ..." from a split summary added to 20a's procedureStackView, so procedureStack.ts stays the one place that decides what the stack says. Price precedence, fixed rate and discount, and the anaesthetist adjustment

Contracts After phase 23 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 13 items covered

Phase 24 puts every Procedure's price through one precedence in src/domain/billing/pricePrecedence.ts, which also records the price source and rejects invalid inputs. The order: office override, then the anaesthetist's typed price (adjustable Contracts only), then the line's fixed price as the whole price, then BTM x the fixed rate or the anaesthetist's unit value, less a locked fixed discount or the anaesthetist's own %. The anaesthetist adjustment and the office override become two separate records. The anaesthetist can adjust only on No contract (RVG) and first-party Contracts; third-party prices are read-only and a fixed discount shows locked. A $0 price gives a no-charge invoice. The rate x time line and its Method 3 gate go, with Aria re-expressed as a $26.50 fixed-rate line.

At authorise, write a pricing snapshot per Procedure (procedure, Contract version id, resolved values and layers, recorded BTM, Booking-level units, rate, discount, price and source, split, payer or billable party), plus the payee and invoice recipe per Booking, all in domain/billing/lock.ts. There is no separate Contract-version store: Phase 18's chain is the history.
- authoriseList writes every Booking's lock (locked or rejected) in the same commit as the state flip, then emits listAuthorised. A refused authorise writes nothing. Every authorise path (Review, the PWA office stand-in, Play the office, scenario jumps, stage-post-op) goes through it. Add no authorise blocker: warnings never block (15a), and the engine's rejections (a Contract not valid on the procedure date, 24's rejections) hold back that Booking only, previewed on Review as advisory flags.
- The engine, retry and regenerate read only the lock, never state.masters. No effective-date fallback, no route or payer resolution, no Resolve & retry that edits a Contract, and never a silent No contract (RVG). Delete contractIneffective, billedAs and any defaultContractFor remnant. The run checks holder references against the locked version (referenceMissing) as the backstop to 21's completion rule.
- The invoice keeps its recipe (US-08.4.4): a locked invoice's document prints its addressee, patient and supplier from the lock, and Regenerate rebuilds it from the stored inputs. Nothing rebuilds an invoice from data as it stood at another point in time.
- The payee is fixed at authorise: the run stamps it on the billing case and the invoice supplier, and handoffCase, receipts, the web accounts and 16's BCTI records read the stamped payee, not a Booking-to-List join. Pre-payment cases keep the join until 27 and 41.
- Failure stays per Booking: a failed or rejected Booking issues none of its invoices (both halves of a split included), its siblings bill, and the List never fails.
- The office's manual fix never edits a master: supplyLockedReference fills a blank, declared holder reference on a failed case (no pricing field), and relockHeldBackBooking sets a Contract valid on the date and re-locks only a held-back Booking that has no invoice. Retry stays idempotent and never duplicates an invoice, case or Xero pair.
- Seeded AUTHORISED Lists get locks at seed time (migrated locks for the history backdrop, labelled, with the payee stamped). No new RNG draws. Bump PERSIST_VERSION once for the seed change.
- Locked Bookings display from the lock in all three apps (fees, the stack's Contract part, Review), with the "Contract vN locked at authorise" badge; ACTIVE Bookings still re-price live. Phase 18's Versions list gains the invoices raised under each version.

  - Register "Regenerate from locked data" (harness bar, Admin invoice document) and re-point Phase 14's "Trigger billing failure" (harness bar, Billing monitor) to the missing claim reference on Losa Tuilagi's COS ACC Booking, in Phase 14's registry.
  - Put the bodies in src/store (stageBillingFailure in src/store/demoStaging.ts) so pwaPurity holds. They must be deterministic, with a disabled state; regenerate is read-only and keeps its result in Phase 14's non-persisted trigger memory for the invoice rail to show.
  - No new PWA entry, but test that the PWA office stand-in locks the List with the handset's anaesthetist as payee. Nothing new goes on the Control Panel page.
- House rules:
  - Every write goes through mutate(), and every new audit code gets a label in src/shared/audit/actionLabels.ts.
  - Keep billing rules pure in src/domain/billing with Vitest tests.
  - Teal is the only action colour; crimson is identity only; the lock badge is a neutral pill, not a status colour.
  - Admin uses panels and overlays; any price an anaesthetist sees on a locked Booking is read-only.
  - No en or em dashes in app copy; never "slot" (say session, AM or PM); "Booking", never "card".
  - Never commit.

While working:
- Invoke the /frontend-design:frontend-design skill before building or reshaping any UI (screens, sheets, dialogs, panels, rows, banners, pills, empty and error states), and apply it inside this repo's design system: the docs/design files and src/theme tokens stay authoritative (convention 17, ROADMAP.md "Front-end design"), so use the skill for layout, hierarchy, spacing, states and finish, never for a new palette, typeface or visual language. Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it.
- The prepaid set is procedures, or whole RVG groups, on Phase 19's ids (procedureTypeIds and rvgGroupIds), never printed codes and never the old AA tag groups. Groups expand at read time through 19's procedureTypesInGroup; explicit procedures survive unticking a group; the stored form is canonical, so an unchanged save writes no audit. A retired id already ticked stays; a retired one cannot be newly ticked.
- Prices are read-only and come from one place: 19a's ownFixedPriceFor and ownPriceListFor in src/domain/billing, for the version in force on the demo date. No price, amount or Contract reference is stored on the profile, no screen reads Contract lines directly, and "No price yet" shows where the anaesthetist's own Contract has no line. There is no anaesthetist write path to any Contract, their own price list included (OQ-91); test that the store refuses it. No pre-payable flag on the Contract (OQ-25).
- One Anaesthetist record, one unit value, one identifier. The profile edits Anaesthetist.unitValue, the field fees read and Phase 25's snapshot copies. A change re-prices only Procedures not yet authorised. Do not add a second copy of the rate. The HPI CPN stays the one hpiId field, labelled "HPI CPN" everywhere (no "HPI id" or "HPI number"), checked with Phase 17's normaliseHpiCpn, isPlausibleHpiCpn and duplicate check. The GST number is Phase 22's field and validator; reuse them.
- Nothing is derived from the prepaid set in this phase. No Booking, banner, gate, warning or review flag reads prepaidSettings; Phase 20's office-set prepaymentRequired flag and bookingRequiresPrepayment stay untouched. Phase 27 does the derivation, the amount on the Booking and OQ-92's warning. Never write "estimate" or "deposit" anywhere.
- Privacy: the profile and its selectors read masters and Contracts only, never the officePrivate slice or a tier or pairing audit entry. Phase 17's officePrivacy.test.ts and pwaPurity.test.ts stay green.
- Build the pure helpers first, with Vitest tests: bank account normalise and mask, the prepaid set (normalise, validate, expand, reason, price rows, summary) in src/domain/billing/prepaidSet.ts, and the profile field policy as data.
- Permissions are enforced in the store. The anaesthetist edits only their own rate, GST period, GST number, contact details and prepaid set. The office edits everything, including bank details, the HPI CPN and active. Nobody edits the registration number. Any role 'system' actor (integration feeds, runs, demo control) edits nothing. Refusals render verbatim.
- Every write goes through mutate() and is audited. Office edits carry onBehalfOf (MutationMeta gains it and mutate() copies it onto the AuditEntry). Bank numbers are masked in the audit and everywhere outside the office's edit field. A no-change save writes no audit entry.
- Admin: extend Phase 17's anaesthetist record page (/admin/masters/anaesthetists/:anaesthetistId) with the Profile, Prepaid procedures and Own price list cards, and link to the Contract in 19a's editor; do not build a second editor or a Contract creation flow.
- Bank details are display-only. The payables run shows each destination account (or a warning-tone "No bank account on file") and snapshots it on the disbursement; it holds, reroutes or re-amounts nothing. No seeded payout changes.
- A GST number edit never changes an invoice already issued (Phase 22's supplier snapshot).
- Mock backend only. Determinism: seeded bank numbers are built from the registration number on non-issued bank code 99, and nothing new draws from the seeded RNG. Bump PERSIST_VERSION once.
- Keep the seed coherent for Phase 27: Souter ticks Rhinoplasty (priced $1,200 on her Contract) and one whole group with priced and unpriced procedures; two colleagues have a set and no price list. The seeded sets, counted only where the Procedure is billed to the payer on the Booking who is a person paying for the patient (21's isPayerBilled and isPersonParty, the pair Phase 27 derives with, D23), must hit exactly the Bookings Phase 20 flagged prepaymentRequired (Nair on the rhinoplasty, not the septoplasty), with Riley's Booking the one noted exception if its procedure is still blank. Change a seeded set, never a Booking's procedure.
- The shared tick list, price list and profile rows live in src/shared/profile and import nothing from apps/, so pwaPurity stays green.
- Design: mobile edits in bottom sheets with a sticky teal Save, never a desktop form; the tick list mirrors the picker's two tabs (Procedures, RVG codes) under body-section headings with one search. The web profile is a desktop layout reached from the persona block, and the four nav tabs are unchanged. Teal is the only action colour, crimson is identity only, and "via", "No price yet", "Retired" and "Not on file" markers are neutral or warning-tone pills. Prices, codes and account numbers are mono.
- No en dashes or em dashes in any app-facing copy.
- Demo triggers: none. Everything is normal use, so add no trigger-registry entry, no 15a warning sample, and leave the Control Panel alone.
- Build nothing ahead of the plan: no prepayment derivation, prepaid amount on a Booking, "no price" warning, price editing, GST schedule rework, payout history, payout hold, bank verification, HPI CPN register lookup or check character (no phase builds them; 40a only unifies the label and format), start date (28) or notifications.
- Keep npm run build, npm run build:pwa and npx vitest run green at the end of the session.

List submit never invoices it again.

Mobile, web, admin and every finder (US-01.4.2) read the same Slot views and the same isOpenSlot, so a session looks the same everywhere and a session holding a List is never offered as free.
- Keep the six-colour design language: DisplayStatusKey is the same six keys, the Slot statuses plus the List kinds are exactly those six, and the theme parity test still holds. List kind (private, public, pre-op) is a List attribute the catalogue does not model: keep it and list it for the owner.
- Generation follows US-01.1.1 (Confirmed) and OQ-81 part 1: only active anaesthetists, from their start date; every new Slot written free; then the anaesthetist's calendar; then recurring bookings. The RNG fill goes on every generated date (rolled days, new anaesthetists, horizon extensions), weekends included. Recurring bookings keep today's weekday-only guard (Phase 30 adds weekend patterns). A recurring booking that meets an unavailable Slot is traced as a clash, not projected (Phase 31 makes it a Draft List).
- The horizon is a setting (FT-01.1): appSettings.schedule.horizonMonths, 4 by default, beside the default AM and PM times, in one schedule-settings record. Every horizon reader goes through horizonFor(today, months). Extending generates the new days; shortening drops far-edge Slots and empty Lists and refuses while a List there holds Bookings.
- Determinism first. Before touching the generator, commit a golden fixture of today's canvas (the demo window 2026-07-07 to 2026-08-16 and the far edge) and seeded Bookings. The seed keeps today's slot-RNG content inside that fixed window as recorded history (seedRecordedWindow, same per-slot draws), so the window and every Booking reproduce exactly; the far-edge section is regenerated once, deliberately, when the RNG fill goes. Projected Lists keep their L-<reg>-<date>-<session> ids (never parsed to find a Slot); runtime Lists take LG####; Slots are S-<reg>-<date>-<session>. Bump PERSIST_VERSION by one and extend the migrate test.
- Start date and active (US-01.1.3, FT-01.1). Anaesthetist gains a required startDateISO; seeded anaesthetists start before the horizon, so the golden fixture holds. No Slot exists before a start date, or from today for an inactive anaesthetist, on any path (seed, Add, Edit, roll-forward, horizon extension). Add generates from the later of the start date and the demo clock's today; editing the date or the active flag adds or removes Slots from today on and refuses when a removed Slot holds a List.
- The Admin Day grid's roster comes from rosterForDate (the anaesthetist master, every anaesthetist with a Slot that day), not the static cast array, so added anaesthetists appear (US-01.4.2). The Day view's date picker is bounded by the horizon, with a "Beyond the schedule horizon" state.
- Delete listForSlot rather than re-implementing it, so the compiler shows every caller (including the Phase 14 registry entries stage-post-op and ingest-pdf-row). Each caller must handle "no List in this Slot": integrations park instead of silently retiming, the post-op addendum creates its List in today's open session (interim until 38b), the PDF picker and the Move Booking picker offer Lists only.
- Session 1 must end green and demoable: the drawer, phone advice, Edit list, Reassign and Add anaesthetist get the minimal re-point the compiler forces (work item 12, "compile-forced minimums"), and session 2 finishes them. Roll-forward and addAnaesthetist read the seed's SEED_LEAVE once masters.availability is gone.
- Assignment needs a surgeon and a hospital and is an office action (US-01.3.3); a closed hospital is flagged on the new List, never blocked. Assigning onto an unavailable or holiday session is refused for now and labelled interim (Phase 30 makes it accept-and-flag). The surgeon picker is 17's SurgeonPicker (not-preferred surgeons in their own group), a not-preferred choice shows 17's NotPreferredWarning with "Assign anyway", and assignListToSlot writes 17's list.pairingAcknowledged for an office actor through notPreferredEntryIds: warn, never block (US-01.3.5, OQ-43). Phone advice now assigns first, so its acknowledgement moves from onBookingCreated to the assignment, written once. Add store/slotActions.ts to officePrivacy.test.ts's allowlist.
- A Slot holding a List that the anaesthetist marks unavailable keeps its List with a conflict flag, labelled interim: Phase 32 builds return to the office or assign to a colleague (US-01.5.5).
- Reassign moves the List between Slots: same id, Bookings and history; target session open; the vacated session returns to Free by default (OQ-84's recommendation, provisional in the Decisions log), with Unavailable or Holiday on request. No absorb, no regenerate. Candidates are open sessions (isOpenSlot) still shown through 17's AnaesthetistCandidates (groups, tier order, shuffle, filter, Preferred pills). Keep 17's acknowledgement for an office move onto a not-preferred pairing, in reassignList (the office entry point), not in moveListToSlot, which Phases 32 and 32a reuse for the anaesthetist's own moves and which must read, check and log no preference (US-01.4.5). A move recalculates no prepayment and no invoice (US-06.3.5, US-06.5.4: an honour system); if any re-check sits on reassignList or reassignBooking, remove it with its tests and log it. Mark moveListToSlot as the seam for Phase 41's payee repoint (OQ-80) and build nothing for it.
- The office availability finder (work item 20; US-01.4.2, US-01.3.5, US-01.3.6): "Find available" in the Admin Day header opens a sheet listing everyone with an open session that day and session, through 17's rankAnaesthetistCandidates and AnaesthetistCandidates only (tier order, shuffled within a tier from a date, session and suggestionSeq key, the tier filter, and with a surgeon chosen the not-preferred group apart); picking a row opens Assign List with that surgeon. Admin only: the mobile and web finders stay name-ordered with no tier or preference, and 17's privacy test stays green.
- Default AM and PM times live in the schedule-settings record; per-Slot overrides live on the Slot and travel with a reassigned List. Remove the four hardcoded duplicates. A session keeps its default shape on the grid even with one Booking (US-01.1.4's note).
- Empty Slots carry no List state. Every List created by assignment or projection is ACTIVE (15b's rename); print states as 15b does (ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED), with no "Open" label; DRAFT and "Draft List" stay free for Phase 31.
- Use the catalogue's words in new copy: "reassign" or "move", not "swap"; "recurring booking" where the catalogue says it (the Permanent List screens are renamed in Phase 30, not here).

Nothing is added to the harness bar or the Control Panel page, because every office action in this phase, the horizon change included, is demoable through the Admin app in the framed build.
- Design: teal the only action colour, crimson unused on the new sheets, Admin sheets through useSurface().Overlay, and no en or em dashes in any app copy.

Add Vitest tests for the Slot module, the generator (order, free by default, active only, clashes), the store actions (refusals, audit, identity, one mechanism, independence from Bookings, horizon, start date, active, roster, three-app and finder parity) and the seed invariants.

Phase goal: the canvas becomes Slots and Lists. Every active anaesthetist has an AM and a PM Slot per day from their start date to the end of a configurable horizon (four months), written free and then painted with their calendar and the surgeons' recurring bookings, with no invented sessions; the status on the Slot is the one mechanism, with no record reconciled into Lists. A List is created only when the office assigns one (or a recurring booking projects it) and then shows in place of the status. The displayed status never depends on Bookings and matches in all three apps and the finders, added anaesthetists appear on the Admin Day grid, default times and the horizon come from one setting, Reassign moves a List between Slots intact with no prepayment re-check, the office's finder lists the available anaesthetists by priority tier with not-preferred pairings apart through Phase 17's helper (never in the anaesthetist apps), every new List is ACTIVE, and the UI never says "slot".

While working:

Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it.
- Mock backend only. Every write goes through a store action and the audited mutate(), with before/after metas and demo-clock timestamps. Components never own domain state. setAvailabilityRange, clearAvailability, createAvailabilitySeries and deleteAvailabilitySeries are each one mutate(), all or nothing on refusal, with one audit entry plus one entry per List affected.
- One mechanism (OQ-27 and OQ-64 answered): the calendar writes the Slot's own status directly. A series is a rule (weekdays, sessions, every 1 to 4 weeks, start, optional until) plus exceptions; it writes its Slots, and a single-instance edit or delete is stored as an exception so no later series write, clock roll forward or horizon extend overwrites it. Nothing reads availability from anywhere but Slots. A series fills only Slots at the default status and in no other series, and reports the rest as left as they are. One helper, seriesCalendarFor, feeds active series (with their exceptions) into 28's generateCanvasForDates as calendar input on every generating path (rollCanvasForward, setHorizonMonths when extending, an earlier start date or a reactivation), so they are painted with the anaesthetist's calendar BEFORE recurring bookings (OQ-81 part 1, settled). A recurring booking on a series-closed session is then never placed: 28's generator returns it as a RecurringClash, which Phase 31 turns into a Draft List. The generator's closed test reads isClosed over the status records; it still draws no RNG. Series rules live in src/domain/availabilitySeries.ts, pure and tested.
- The Slot status set becomes a user-maintained master list (masters.slotStatuses, US-01.2.2), availability values only. Each status has a fixed internal ID (SlotStatusKey) that rules read, never its label; seeded IDs are 28's stored values (free, holiday, unavailable), and an added status gets a generated ST#### ID, shown read only and never edited. Label, long label, description, colour (one of the six design tokens) and treatment are editable, plus "open for bookings" and "anaesthetists can set". Seed the owner's starting set: Free (default, dashed), Holiday (long label "On holiday") and Unavailable (hatched), with today's colours. No "available for emergency" and no extra kinds of unavailable seeded; an admin can add them (Greg: several kinds of unavailable, same effect). A rename or recolour shows in every view with every rule unchanged, and an added status works with no code change (US-01.2.2's two criteria; test both). No provisional line anywhere.
- The List types (private, public, pre-op) stay a fixed List attribute with their own tokens, so a session holding a List shows the List in its place with the design's List colours; no status ID can equal a List kind. Log on the "For the owner's review" list that the catalogue has no List kind.
- Availability is not the List's state (US-01.2.2 since 2026-10-07): the status master, the display key, the legends and the filters never hold DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED. ListState and its chip stay on the List, untouched. validateSlotStatusDraft refuses a label or long label that is a List state or its label (plus "Draft" and "Draft List", ready for Phase 31), the Availability statuses header says this is a session's availability, not a List's state (Draft, Active, Submitted, Authorised), and the table marks rows "In use" or "Retired", never "Active". Log the guard on the "For the owner's review" list.
- The only closed sets left are the palette (the six Design Language status tokens in src/theme/statusColours.ts, same hexes) and the List types. No new hex anywhere. The hatched and dashed treatments generalise with tokens only, and today's exact strings must still come out for the seeded statuses and every List.
- No literal availability keys outside src/domain/slotStatus.ts and the seed. Finders, filters, counts and clashes use isOpenForBooking, isClosed and isOpenSlot. Only what counts as free changes: the office finder's priority-tier ordering, its not-preferred group and Phase 17's soft not-preferred warning (wired in by 28) stay as they are, and the anaesthetists' own finders stay untiered.
- Availability is never merged into the List. A List in a Slot shows in place of the status. The clash comes from one pure function, availabilityClash: a bookable status clears that List's availability conflict and raises nothing; a closed status over a List flags it once, replacing rather than stacking, with the List's surgeon, hospital, Bookings, times and List type untouched. That flag is the interim for one settled rule, Phase 32's return-or-assign (US-01.5.5) when an anaesthetist marks a session holding a List unavailable; its doc comment says so, and says generation never reaches it (a recurring booking on a closed session is traced as 28's clash for Phase 31's Draft List, not placed and flagged). Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it.
- Mock backend only. Every write goes through a store action and the audited mutate(), with before and after metas and timestamps from the demo clock. Components never own domain state. The writes are create, assign, re-date and remove for Draft Lists, the recurring clash, Bookings added to and moved off them through the existing Booking actions, and the pairing refusals.
- The DRAFT state. ListState becomes 'DRAFT' | 'ACTIVE' | 'SUBMITTED' | 'AUTHORISED', and List is a union on it: AssignedList (ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED, with an anaesthetist and a Slot) and DraftList (DRAFT, no anaesthetist, no Slot, a draft trail). LIST_STATE_LABELS gains DRAFT, shown only on a Draft List beside "Unassigned"; no assigned List reads "DRAFT" or "Open". Only an ACTIVE List can be completed and submitted; submitting or authorising a Draft List refuses with "Assign an anaesthetist first.". A store-wide invariant test holds FT-07.1: every ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED List has its anaesthetist, Slot, day, session, hospital and surgeon, and every DRAFT List has neither anaesthetist nor Slot.
- A Draft List is a List record, plus a draft trail (origin, source, since, by, and for a recurring clash the day it stands for). There is no separate collection, so its Bookings hang off its List id and assignment keeps the id.
  - createDraftList and the recurring clash write through one insertDraftList and leave schedule.slots and every other List untouched; prove it with a test.
  - Only assignDraftList takes DRAFT to ACTIVE, through attachListToSlot, in the session its day and session fix (the admin chooses only the anaesthetist), in one commit with a draftList.assign meta (before state DRAFT, after ACTIVE); the draft trail is kept with assignedAtISO. 15a's warnings are derived on read (store/warnings.ts), so they need no call, but their rules and OpenWarningRow must tolerate a Booking on a Draft List.
  - An ACTIVE List only becomes a Draft List through detachListToDraft, built and unit-tested here for Phase 32 (origins movedToOffice and unavailableReturn); it refuses a SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED List, and no screen in this phase calls it.
  - removeDraftList soft-removes and refuses while it holds an active Booking; redateDraftList moves it and its Bookings to another day and keeps its waiting time.
  - A Draft List cannot be submitted, authorised or billed, and an anaesthetist cannot add a Booking to one.
  - No projection, roll forward or new-anaesthetist path may overwrite a List id a Draft List holds, and a recurring booking never projects a second List or Draft List for a day it already answered for (the Draft List keeps recurringBookingId, and a recurring clash keeps the day in draft.projectedFor even after a re-date or a removal).
- Prepayment (US-06.3.5, US-06.5.4, D20). A Booking on a Draft List has no anaesthetist, so 27's routine generates and withdraws nothing for it. Built default, logged for the owner: the first assignment of a Booking that never had an anaesthetist is its setup, so assignDraftList runs 27's routine (syncPrepayment) once for it with the listAssigned cause 27's plan exports for this call (use the name 27 shipped); reassigning a List that already had an anaesthetist (one Phase 32 returned), re-dating and detaching re-trigger nothing (honour system; the payee repoint is Phase 41's, D38).
- The recurring clash (OQ-81 part 2, built as the answer): one pure recurringClashDraft turns each clash (Phase 28's generator RecurringClash or Phase 30's skipped entry: a recurring booking covering a closed session) into a DRAFT Draft List with the recurring booking's hospital, surgeon, kind and notes, origin recurringClash and a stable derived id. It runs on every path that yields clashes: addRecurringBooking, editRecurringBooking, applyRecurringBookingsToCanvas ("Apply to canvas now"), every roll forward, the horizon extend, an earlier start date, and the seed's generation. Confirm 29 paints series onto new Slots before recurring bookings (seriesCalendarFor in the generator's calendar step), so no recurring booking is ever left flagged on the anaesthetist; if any path still places and then flags, fix it (work item 9). Never for a past day. It writes no availability conflict and never shows on Conflicts for the anaesthetist (US-01.5.4 AC3); a hospital closure still raises Phase 30's holiday conflict. An edit, retire or move of the recurring booking updates or removes an empty clash Draft List and keeps one with Bookings. Phase 30's sheet wording for skipped sessions now says they go to Draft Lists.
- Phase 17's helper, privately (US-01.3.5, US-01.3.6, D44). The assign picker is draftListAvailability (free, not available, occupied; no preference knowledge) ranked once by 17's rankAnaesthetistCandidates and split into Free, "Not preferred with Ms Reid", Not available and Already has a List (disabled), each tier-ordered and shuffled within a tier (requestKey from the List id and suggestionSeq), with 17's tier filter, Preferred pills and an Everyone / Free only toggle. assignDraftList writes list.pairingAcknowledged (through notPreferredEntryIds) only for a not-preferred pairing. Add store/draftListActions.ts to the allowlist in 17's officePrivacy.test.ts as an office write path; it must not import store/officePrivate.ts, so the PWA closure check stays green. The PWA stand-in skips a not-preferred pairing through draftListFitsAnaesthetist, a boolean, and never names a preference or a tier. No inline preference checks or sorts anywhere.
- Warn, never block, except for the real guards:
  - A closed session (Unavailable, Holiday or any closed status) or a not-preferred choice is selectable, warned before save, and assigned. A closed session gets a conflict through Phase 30's path and its warning tells the office to check with the anaesthetist (US-01.4.7); a not-preferred pairing gets 17's acknowledgement entry.

Phase goal: a List with no anaesthetist is a Draft List, the first state (DRAFT) of a List's lifecycle. Each has a hospital, surgeon, day and session, all required, may already hold Bookings, and takes no Slot. Draft Lists are flagged "Unassigned" with their waiting time and sorted soonest first, beside the day in the right rail, in a band on the Day dashboard, on their own Admin page and on a nav badge. Only the office assigns one, by choosing the anaesthetist from everyone potentially available, grouped and tier-ordered by Phase 17's helper with soft warnings and a full audit, and it becomes ACTIVE; or the office removes it or changes its date. A recurring booking that lands on a session the anaesthetist has already marked unavailable becomes a Draft List. Every List has exactly one hospital and one surgeon, and the Day dashboard shows each block's booking count.

From the Booking, "Move to a colleague" finds the receiver by name, offers only colleagues whose session is available (someone on leave sets it available first, which is their acceptance), and lands the Booking at once on the colleague's matching List or a List created in their session. Hospital download and the matching screen

Intake After phases NaN, 31 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 10 items covered

Hospital bookings and feed messages become rows on an Admin matching screen. Each row shows its procedure text exactly as received, plus its change type and field differences. A later update to a matched Booking is matched by date, surgeon, hospital and session, then waits for approval. The office matches a row, creates a Booking, a List or a Draft List that holds it, or rejects it. Unmatched rows wait in a queue. Nothing applies by itself. Created Bookings keep the wording and wait for the office to set their Contract.

- Draft-then-save is Admin only. Mobile, web and the PWA mount no draft provider and keep their immediate saves exactly as today; the anaesthetist never calls saveBookingChanges.
- Nothing on the Admin Booking detail may bypass the draft. Drafted edits go through the booking-store context; commands (complete, uncomplete, cancel, move, the prepayment, event and invoice actions where built, and the update email) act on the real store and are disabled while there are unsaved changes. A drafted action may touch only the snapshot's slices and never emit an app event (the emitter is shared by every store); a demo Reset discards a dirty draft. Add the source-scanning test that enforces it. In draft mode, sheet buttons read Apply, not Save.
- One save is one change set: one change-set id across the entries, a booking.save header, the office as the actor. The lastModified stamps never appear in audit before or after. A save applies the admin's own changes onto the real Booking as it is at Save time, reading each before value from it; a cancel, move or authorise in between blocks it with a plain reason. No row versions, merge or clash prompt: concurrent edits (US-02.5.6) are Future Work. Remap draft-created ids against the real counters and re-check the existing invariants through their own guards (22's resolveSplit, one primary Procedure, 20's contractCandidatesFor, 24's price-precedence rejections, the source texts only appended, validateNhi). A blank procedure or a missing Contract never refuses a save (D33). A save that changed the Procedures, a Contract or the payer runs 27's re-check once on the real store (one prepayment invoice with its ledger pair and draft Xero pair, never two); in the draft store it is a no-op; a move never re-checks (D20).
- The wording as received is never edited (US-02.5.7, 20a). On an amend the office adds wording as given beside it through 20a's Add wording as given (Told by Phone or Email), which in draft mode is a drafted append applied at Save by 20a's append rules; a draft that changed an existing text refuses; editProcedure is never handed sourceTexts.
- Every List owner change (28's reassignment, 31's assignment, 32's moves, whichever app makes them) carries a listReassign change set and shows in the History of the List's Bookings; a List reassignment is its own event, not a save, and its flow keeps no email step (US-01.4.1).

It starts from the admin-maintained template for the kind of change (Change of anaesthetist, Cancellation, Correction of an error, Booking change), editable in Master data. Opening the mail client writes one "Update email drafted (not sent)" entry and nothing else; nothing is stored or labelled as sent. Only the allowlisted fields appear (the procedure by its procedure-list name): never an NHI, date of birth, internal notes, the wording as received, the RVG code, Contract or holder, payer or insurance indication, modifiers and explanations, money, or pairing preferences and tiers (17's office-private slice), and a List email names no patient. No move, List or Booking, held or sent, changes any pair (D20's honour system: nothing detects or re-checks a move). There is no prepaid excess and no balance invoice: a prepaid Procedure is priced at the prepaid amount and nothing is raised automatically afterwards (US-06.4.1, OQ-61), so add no excess field anywhere. - Both legs move together. A receipt updates received and released in one commit, through Phase 16's payableReleasedFor, never a second copy. Nothing disburses above released, and cumulative leg amounts always equal the sums of their entries.
- The ledger maths is pure, in src/domain/billing/ledger.ts, with Vitest tests. The imbalance is receipts held less payables due, exact to the cent. AA fee money (AA's own, never netted against payables) and held prepayments are never part of it. The per-anaesthetist positions plus the unattributed held receipts sum to the whole ledger, anaesthetistsOutOfBalance lists exactly the anaesthetists whose scoped imbalance is non-zero or who have a check, and the seed is in balance with that list empty.
- No app money view (web, mobile, admin, shared) reads state.xero. An unmatched receipt is held in the ledger, and only the office clears it, by allocating or refunding it. A receipt whose bank reference names an anaesthetist carries that anaesthetistId and puts them out of balance until cleared; one naming no one counts only in the whole ledger.

Xero mirror resilience and the processing monitor

Money After phase 36 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 4 items covered

Xero mirror becomes a fallible integration while Phase 36's ledger stays the system of record. Disbursement is detected from Xero (bill-paid webhook or poll) and no longer performed by the engine. Bulk remittance is matched only on the simulated Xero side. A demo-clock outage queue with backoff drains without duplicates. Voids and amendments made in Xero are flagged at the poll. The Billing monitor (US-13.3.1) is restyled for a large list: grouped by anaesthetist, sort and filter, Problems only, URL state, and "Open in Review" on SUBMITTED Lists, with approval kept on Review.

Only recordDisbursement writes the payable leg's disbursement, through Phase 36's pure applyDisbursement and a LedgerDisbursement extended with its idempotency key and detectedBy (no second disbursement map). One attempt per item per clock change; no timers (do not copy wireIntegrationRetry's setTimeout), no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(). Authorising a List is never blocked by Xero. Restoring Xero drains in order with no duplicate pair, contact, receipt or disbursement.

- Mock backend only, through store actions and the audited mutate(). The original Booking, its Procedures, its lock and pricing snapshots and the original invoice are never written: "Credit waiting for review", "Credited" and every link are derived selectors.
- A credit is an event on 38b's element (a new kind, its label in 38b's one label place; EVENT_KINDS.credit with addedBy office and anaesthetist, anaesthetistOwnOnly, reviewed). The credit event and its replacements (38b additional invoices) are submitted, reviewed and issued as one correction: one row in 38b's review queue (naming who raised it), no second queue, and issued together inside 38b's runEventInvoicing commit (its generic loop skips replacements; its handoff loop sends a correction to handoffCorrection, never handoffPair). liveInvoiceForProcedure skips a credited invoice and returns its live replacement. Compute the reversal plan from the legs at issue time. Nothing but a person's action raises a credit (US-06.4.1).
- Who may credit: the office on any Procedure; the anaesthetist on their own Procedure only, through 38b's mayRaise and procedureOwner, enforced in the store (notOwnProcedure) as well as the UI, reached through 38a's archive or search. The anaesthetist's form shows the original's number, party and total and "Your payment for this invoice is reversed.", lets them add new invoices, and has no split, no copy and no ledger figures. Its office review on the PWA is the PWA-only stand-in "Office reviews this credit" (office-reviews-credit, body in src/store), following 38b's office-reviews-additional-invoice, which must skip replacement events.
- The credit note option credits the original in full to any billable party (default the original's, the choice audited), with a reason, and zero or more replacements; "Credit in full and rebill" (the office's) opens with one replacement to the original's party, which from session 2 holds a copy of the original's lines and holder references (US-08.6.6; each line at quantity 1 for its stored ex-GST amount, negative lines such as 27's prepayment deduction folded into the line they follow, so the copy totals the original exactly and passes priceFreeFormInvoice). A rebill's total is whatever the correction needs: the equal-total rule is the split's only. A credit note is not a refund: no money moves and nothing pays a held credit out. A rebill never re-prices from a Contract, never rewrites the Booking's lock and pays the locked payee.
- On issue, one engine commit: the credit note, the receivable credit, a negative invoice to the anaesthetist on every credit (the payable is always reversed: the undisbursed part offset, the paid-out part left as its recoveryDue for 39a to net in the weekly run), and the replacements through 38b's issue path with the rebillOf lineage; then one Xero commit (reversal and every new pair together, with the fault path and an idempotent retry; 38b's own handoff never runs twice for a replacement). Payments on a credited ACCREC, payables over a reversed ACCPAY (through 37's payBillsInXero too, if 37 ran) and a late handoff of a credited invoice are refused. runPayables does not net the negative invoice. No Xero credit note carries an NHI, a patient name or other personal information (OQ-30).
- The split (US-08.6.4) is the same flow with cause 'split', office only, only on a Procedure on a combination Contract once its invoice exists: at least two replacements prefilled from combinationParts (allow cards beyond the parts, since a single-parent combination returns one), each with its own party and a freely typed amount, which must add up to the credited invoice ex GST to the cent (splitTotalCheck, pure, in the store too; per-invoice GST rounding accepted and shown), with a live Left to allocate figure and Submit disabled until it is $0.00. A prepaid combination's split, and any credit on a prepayment invoice, stay refused (they need Phase 41's credit of a prepayment invoice): record them as known gaps against US-08.6.4 and US-08.6.5 and hand them to 41.
- Billing maths is pure and tested in src/domain/billing (creditNote.ts with CREDIT_RULES, creditInFull, reversalPlan, splitTotalCheck, xeroCorrectionPlan and rebillDraftFrom, and the credit path added to 36's ledger.ts: applyCredit, and ledgerPosition's equation extended with creditsHeldForPayers and recoveryDueFromAnaesthetists, the names Phases 39a and 41 already plan against; keep them, with NegativeInvoice's amount, cause and recoveryDue), so a credited ledger shows zero imbalance while 36's pinned uncredited figures do not move. Money After phases 37, 39 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 5 items covered

Weekly ISO-week payment cycle (Friday close with snapshot and bank reconciliation, Monday holds that roll forward, office approval of the week's BCTIs, Tuesday schedule), payment only of approved unheld lines, negatives netted per anaesthetist (never below zero), remittance advice in Admin and web Accounts, week shown on every payment; OQ-71 case left outside the system

  • Phase 39's 'Stage refund after payout', then the week's run shows the negative netted on the remittance advice (for example 19 positives and 1 negative, seeded)

No carry-forward recovery invoice and no 'Stage departed anaesthetist' trigger (OQ-71). Phase 41's trust hold keeps held prepayment payables out of a run: leave the hook. Phase 37's 'Pay anaesthetist in Xero' detection must agree with the run's record. Re-baseline any S4 Beat 5 figure the run changes. Demo guide: S4 Beat 5 (partial payment and payout) narrates the weekly run and the remittance advice; the cheat sheet's payables lines.
