While working:
- Invoke the /frontend-design:frontend-design skill before building or reshaping any UI (screens, sheets, dialogs, panels, rows, banners, pills, empty and error states), and apply it inside this repo's design system: the docs/design files and src/theme tokens stay authoritative (convention 17, ROADMAP.md "Front-end design"), so use the skill for layout, hierarchy, spacing, states and finish, never for a new palette, typeface or visual language. Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it. Here it applies to the Billing monitor's payment cycle panel (the step rail, the waiting table, the Monday anomalies with Hold out and Mark fixed, the runs list), the run detail and its payment schedule, the remittance advice document, the Ledger's Payment runs card and caption, the week labels on payments, and the web Remittances tab, sheet and still-to-net panel.
- Mock backend only, through store actions and the audited mutate(). The ledger (Phase 36) stays the system of record and the engine never performs a disbursement: the week's schedule is paid in Xero (the accountant, simulated), and the engine records each bill payment (37's recordDisbursement) and each credit allocation (the new recordOffset) only when Xero reports it, by webhook, poll or the outage queue, idempotent by key.
- The weekly cycle is US-10.2.7: one run per ISO week, named "Week 30"; the office closes the week (the snapshot of released, unpaid payables, the ledger at close, and the reconciliation against the simulated bank download), works the Monday anomalies (hold out of this run, rolling the line into the next week tagged "Rolled from Week 30", or mark fixed), approves the week's BCTIs, and sends the payment schedule to the accountant. A payable released after the close belongs to the next week. Every payment shows the week of the run it was paid in. The demo clock does not gate the steps (it is fixed on Tue 21 Jul, ISO week 30, and forward-only): each step works in order on any day, shows its planned date from the setting and stamps the clock's actual time; the cycle never advances the clock. Log that as a built default for the owner.
- The approval gate is the point of US-10.2.6: no path pays a payable that is not an unheld line of an approved, scheduled run (runPayables, disbursePayable, the Xero-side bill payment, the Xero pair trigger, a replay, the poll, the queue). Approval refuses while a Monday anomaly is open. The one-click demo payouts approve first so the gate has no back door: the Xero sim's "Simulate payment and payout" (S3 Beat 3) and the payout half of 39's "Stage refund after payout" go through approveAndPayPairForDemo (a one-pair staged run beside the week's run, never doubling with it), and 36's PWA "Office runs payables" becomes "Office runs this week's payment cycle" (no "payables" in the label: 14's demoTriggers.test.ts rule, as 36 narrowed it to bar entries with a companion assertion that the only "payables" label is this PWA stand-in; update that companion assertion to the label set as shipped, and keep the bar rule passing as 37 left it with its "Pay anaesthetist in Xero (payables run)" entry). A run is frozen at approval; a stale run is superseded by a Re-close, never edited.
- Netting is pure billing maths in src/domain/billing/payablesRun.ts, and the week, the cycle's days, the reconciliation and the anomalies in src/domain/billing/paymentCycle.ts, both with Vitest worked examples, including US-10.2.5's 19 positives and one negative and its remittance advice criterion, US-10.2.7's held line rolling into the next week, and ISO weeks at year ends (2026 has 53). Netting uses each negative invoice's recoveryDue (what 39 left open), never its offsetAmount, and only unheld lines. Net per anaesthetist is never below zero; what a run cannot net stays open on the negative invoice and nets in a later week with positives. An anaesthetist with only negatives is not in a run. The offset is its own amount on the payable leg (offsetAmount), never counted as cash, and the whole ledger stays in balance after the close, approval, sending and detection.
- OQ-71 (answered): a negative with no later payment is handled outside the system. The only surface is the open amount on the anaesthetist's ledger position with one caption ("If no later payment comes, AA settles it with the anaesthetist outside the system") and the web still-to-net panel. No carry-forward, recovery or write-off wording or record; "Rolled from" and "Rolls into" are only for held lines.
- runExclusionFor is the only standing exclusion point. Today it excludes nothing: 26's bank details are display-only, so a missing account is a Monday anomaly the office holds out or marks fixed, never an automatic exclusion; if 37 shipped a heldForBank refusal, it becomes the first reason; Phase 41 adds 'heldInTrust' there. A Monday hold is a per-week decision on the run's line, not an exclusion. Netting reads every open negative whatever its credit note's cause and whoever raised it.
- The 20th-of-the-month payment is not part of this cycle (Greg: the separate monthly non-trust cycle, Phase 16's AA fee run); build nothing for it and put it on the owner's review list.
- Time from the demo clock only, date-fns over given dates for ISO weeks; no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(). The staging bodies are deterministic.
- Seeded disbursements become backdrop weekly runs (one per ISO week, closed, approved and scheduled before paid) and every seeded receipt gets its bank line, with no figure moving: assert Dr Souter's position, the whole ledger, the GST schedule and S3's figures are identical before and after. The payouts nearest today (15 and 16 Jul) fall in Week 29, so the monitor opens on Week 30 with no run yet. Bump PERSIST_VERSION once for the new slices, setting, bank lines, leg field and backdrop runs, and extend the migrate and seed tests.
- Demo triggers go through the Phase 14 registry, shown only on their screen, with disabled states and bodies in src/store or src/shared: new "Stage a payment week" on the Billing monitor (choices "19 BCTIs" and "19 BCTIs and a credit after payout", service dates before the canvas horizon start, payments through the ordinary webhook with their bank lines, the credit built by one pure credit-after-payout fixture builder over 39's pure credit functions) and "Stage a bank mismatch" (session 2); re-point Phase 39's "Stage refund after payout" (payout through a staged run, result text), Phase 37's "Pay anaesthetist in Xero (payables run)" and Phase 36's PWA stand-in. Close the week, Hold out of this run, Mark fixed, Return to run, Approve week N's BCTIs, Send payment schedule, Re-close and Run payables in Xero are product buttons, not registry entries. Nothing is added to the Control Panel page. No new PWA entry is needed (the cycle, schedule and remittance advice are in Admin and web Accounts; mobile Balances is unchanged, a built default for the owner's review list); confirm the re-pointed stand-in works in the PWA build and pwaPurity.test.ts stays green.
- Every new audit action gets an ACTION_LABELS entry and the right actor (office for the close, holds, fixes, approval and schedule; the office stand-in for staged runs; system for detection; demo for the Xero-side batch payment and the bank lines).
- Follow the design files: teal is the only action colour, crimson stays identity only, pills use semantic tokens, amounts, weeks and dates are mono with tabular-nums, negatives render "-$X.XX" through formatSignedCurrency (neutral, never red), weekday names come from the setting through one helper. No en or em dashes in any app copy.
- Keep npm run build, npm run build:pwa and npx vitest run green throughout, and at the session 1 checkpoint after work item 9 (patch S4 Beat 5 for the cycle's steps before stopping there).

Phase goal: payments to anaesthetists run on a weekly cycle named by its ISO week, which the office closes (snapshot and bank reconciliation), checks (anomalies held out and rolled into the next week), approves (the week's BCTIs, before anything is paid) and schedules for the accountant, who pays it in Xero; each anaesthetist's negative invoices are netted against their positive payables, paid as one net amount and shown on a remittance advice in Admin and web Accounts; every payment shows the week it was paid in; and a negative with no later payment to net against is left to AA to settle outside the system, visible on the anaesthetist's ledger position.

No event, late line or review writes the Booking, its Procedures, their billing lines after submit, or the lock (US-07.3.2). editRefusal stays exactly as it is; 38b's event guard, extended, lets the Procedure's owner (38b's procedureOwner) or the office add, edit or remove unreviewed pre-op and post-op events on any List from ACTIVE to billed; a Draft List (no anaesthetist) refuses.
- An event has its own date and start time and records either a time or a fixed fee, with no modifiers or base units; an invoice tick (cleared: recorded, never invoiced); a billable party by a "same as" tick or, cleared, entered through 21's party picker. Before the List is authorised, ticked events are reviewed in the List's review and, at authorise, priced, frozen and put on the Procedure's invoice as their own lines (same party) or approved to wait for the next run (another party); after it, 38b's review step (the Events tab, EventReviewSheet, approve or decline) applies. 38b's Events tab leaves out events whose List is not yet authorised, so no event has two review paths. Every event's own invoice is raised only by 38b's runEventInvoicing (the next run), from the frozen pricing, traceable to the Procedure and the original invoice, with 36's pair to the locked payee. One path raises each, once. A noEventRate or contractNotInForce event is left for review and priced there with a reason.
- Pricing is pure and tested in src/domain/billing/prePostOpEvent.ts: a time is RVG time units (19a's timeUnitsFromMinutes with the stored rule, rounded up per D25) at the rate and less the discount that 24's calculated step uses (the line's fixed rate, else the anaesthetist's unit value; the line's fixed discount), through one exported helper that priceProcedure also calls, never a second derivation; it reads the Procedure's Contract version in force on the event's date, live, recorded in the frozen pricing, never the Booking's lock; nothing is calculated on a Procedure priced at a Contract fixed price (US-05.2.5); a Contract event fee replaces the time; the ACC pre-op prices from its code fee on the fixed-fee ACC Contract; the anaesthetist's own adjustment never applies to an event. 18's parity fixture and 24's parity must match unchanged (never run them with -u).
- The Contract event fee (ContractEventFee: Contract version, event type, holder code and description, fixed price ex GST) is this phase's one addition to the draft design: one type beside 19a's lines in src/domain/billing, office-only add, edit and remove, copied with a new Contract version, and isPlainRvgContract gains "and has no event fees" so 20's picker never offers a Contract that holds only event fees.
- A billing line gains a date and a preset type and stays 24's fixed amount line, not offered on a fixed-price Procedure; an anaesthetist's line on a List that is not ACTIVE is recorded as an event (addLateBillingLine), never written to the Procedure. The ACC caption in the add-billing-line sheet goes; post-op reviews and pain consults are offered as events too. No UNIT x RATE, add-on or quantity option anywhere.

Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it.
- Mock backend only, and the ledger is the truth. The patient record's invoices and balances read Phase 36's patientLedgerPosition (with 39's credited state and held credit) through store selectors, never state.xero. Seeded backdrop history counts on the patient record but stays off the office's Invoices list and monitor.
- The record's balance is patient-centric (US-13.2.2): every invoice for the patient's procedures counts, whoever pays (the patient, a person paying for them, a hospital, an insurer, ACC), net of credits held, with a by-payer breakdown and a separate "Billed to the patient" figure that the warning reads.
- One record per patient: the patient id (the existing hidden internal id) is the key and the NHI a second unique index (US-11.1.1, which already Matches; the record's ethnicity and details-differ prompt are presentation, not coverage). No path may create a second record for an NHI. Only the office (or the PWA stand-in) attaches an NHI, from Missing NHI, the patient record, or a matching-screen apply-to-existing decision on a row that carries it. Attaching an NHI that already exists merges the provisional record into it in one audited mutate and one action (no separate merge screen): every Booking, ledger pair (a prepayment pair from 27 included), invoice or credit-note counterparty naming the patient, and follow-up is re-pointed (21's Booking.payer of kind patient holds no id and follows the Booking; a person payer and Invoice.billedTo snapshots are left alone), the provisional row is deleted, and a redirect is kept. Details that differ are held for the office to review, never written over the record.
- The NHI is required (D11, still open though AA leans to mandatory; built as the default and labelled provisional, with the rule in one place). A Booking without one goes ahead flagged: it can be created, it is listed on Missing NHI, and authoriseBlockersFor gains an nhiMissing blocker, so the List cannot be authorised. Submission and completion are not blocked. The office simulation and the PWA "Office authorises this List" inherit the refusal. The Missing NHI rows escalate mild then strong as the List date nears, 27's pattern.
- "NHI missing" is the only label for the state, from nhiBadge, on every surface. "NHI pending" disappears. The anaesthetist sees the NHI or "NHI missing", and never patient money or the balance warning.
- The patient balance is a rule in 15a's warning routine (OQ-41 and OQ-74 answered, D24), not a separate alert store. It checks a Booking only when its payer on the Booking is the patient (checksPatientBalance over 21's Booking.payer, the one gate; the Contract does not gate it, and a payer changed to a guardian through setBookingPayer removes it at the next evaluation), and it counts only invoices billed to the patient themself (hospital, insurer, other holder, named-payer 'payer', AA fee and credited invoices never count as owing; the Booking's own invoices, its prepayment invoice included, are excluded). Owing within the threshold is a mild (yellow) warning (the 30-day case is mild, not silent); strictly older than the threshold is strong (red); a credit held for the patient with nothing owing is mild; the age counts from the invoice date in one function (invoiceAgeDays). It is before-procedure (our reading, logged), office-audience only (add an audience field to 15a's WarningRule, default all, so every other rule still shows in both apps per US-13.7.3), and never blocks: staff go ahead and Clear it from the to-do list. There is no submit confirm step to filter (US-13.7.3 dropped it). Only Bookings stamped with balanceCheck at create or match (every createBooking path, the matching screen's apply-to-existing decision, PDF update-by-NHI and the NHI merge, each inside its own commit) carry it; strength is derived live, so a payment or a threshold change applies at the next evaluation. Remove patientHasOutstandingPriorEpisode and the "Prior balance" pill; the monitor shows 15a's triangle.
- The threshold is the rule's thresholdDays param in 15a's appSettings (90), editable by the office in one Master data field, "Patient balance warning after N days", and audited, because US-11.3.2 asks for it; a change applies at the next Booking check. Build nothing else of the settings page (no switches, no other thresholds; US-13.7.4 is Future) and log the tension for the owner.
- Follow-ups (call, note, reminder, resend) are stored, office-only and audited (DM-23's follow-up part, the former DM-47). Resend goes through Phase 22's resendInvoice and appends to the invoice's send history instead of refusing a second send. The NHI request email is a real mailto link built with Phase 35's builder, allowlisted: no DOB, no NHI, no money, no notes.
- Pure rules (invoiceAgeDays, countsTowardPatientBalance, patientBalanceSummary, patientBalanceStrength, missingNhiStrength, detailDifferences, buildNhiIndex) live in src/domain/patients with Vitest tests. Time comes from the demo clock only; no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(); the PWA stand-in's synthetic NHI is deterministic.

Prepayment letters, settlement by hand, trust account and refunds

Prepayment After phases 27, NaN, 39 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 9 items covered

Prepayment letters that state the prepaid amount as the price, plus reminders. Nothing is settled automatically: additional invoices and credit notes (including a provisional part credit) are raised by hand. Prepayments are held in trust until authorise, refunded in full on cancellation, and on a move only the payable's payee is repointed (provisional). A rebook gets a fresh prepayment at the new anaesthetist's own price.

- OQ-40: prepayment money is held in trust and its payable is never released or paid before the List is AUTHORISED, then it goes to 25's lock payee and is paid in 39a's next weekly run; a cancellation refunds in full. OQ-42 and D21: under the hold there is nothing to recover from an anaesthetist, so add no recovery path.
- D20 (superseded 2026-10-08: the honour system) and D38 (OQ-80's default): a prepaid Booking moved to another anaesthetist, by any path (the office's Booking move and List reassign, 31's Draft List assign, 32's List moves, 32a's single-Booking move), is not billed again, nothing is re-checked or recalculated, and only the payee of the prepayment's payable (the ledger's payable leg and the draft ACCPAY) is repointed; the receivable half (the prepayment invoice and the ACCREC) never changes. One store action, repointPrepaymentPayable, called from the one move hook 32 and 32a left (route the office's moves through it), with one doc comment naming D38, OQ-80 and D20 and one "Provisional (OQ-80)" caption on the panel's payee line. Flip 32a's pinned-payee test. There is no agreed-rate settlement: 27 prices the moved prepaid Procedure at the prepaid amount whoever does it.
- One path each. Every credit goes through Phase 39's credit path: the by-hand credit through submitCredit and 38b's review; the cancellation refund as a 39 credit event with the wider cause 'prepaymentRefund', issued in the refund's own commit through 39's issueCreditInto, the confirmed refund dialog being its review step (log that reading for the owner), with 39's applyCredit and handoffCorrection. The hold extends 16's payableReleasedFor and adds 'heldInTrust' to 39a's runExclusionFor; never a second release rule or run filter. The ledger equation gains one heldInTrust term; refundsPaid comes off receipts held while the held credit is marked refunded.
- Money is conserved. The ledger equation and the trust identity hold to the cent after every step; a refund never exceeds what was received; a part credit reverses exactly its amount; nothing is netted or recovered from an anaesthetist for a prepayment; a negative group without a prepayment line still fails with negativeTotal; the locked prepaid price is never altered.
- Every refund links to the original prepayment invoice and names the payable's payee at refund time. A cancellation always refunds the full amount received; unpaid invoices are credited, not refunded. A cancel is never refused because of a prepayment. Only cancellation refunds are paid out of the trust account.
- The rebook is for a true cancellation only. It creates a new Booking through createBooking (Copy a Booking is gone), on the replacement's own first-party Contract when they have a price for the procedure (else none, so 20's and 27's "needs a Contract" and "price needed" take over), and lets Phase 27's engine generate the fresh prepayment at their own fixed price, held for Approve and send. Nothing moves between anaesthetists. Seed Dr Beaumont's own price list (Rhinoplasty $1,350.00) through 19a's seed.
- Letters are plain-text templates that must state the prepaid amount as the price (validator: {{prepaidAmount}} required in a request template, and "estimate", "deposit" or "may be higher or lower" refused); a template may say a further invoice or credit is possible. Rendered when an admin approves and sends, snapshotted on the invoice, with no NHI. The letter module and the trust view are pure in src/domain/billing with Vitest tests; names come from src/shared/format.ts. This phase builds no pricing structure: the prepaid amount and price step stay in 27's prepayment.ts and 24's pricePrecedence.ts.
- Every mutation goes through mutate() with audit and the right actor. Refunds, payouts, reminders, rebooks and template edits are office only; the by-hand credit and additional invoice are the office's or the anaesthetist's on their own Procedure; the release runs as the billing run and the repoint as the billing engine; the bank settles a payout as a system actor. Time comes from the demo clock: no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random().
- Keep the filler generator's rng() draw order unchanged and bump PERSIST_VERSION once per session that changes the seed.
- Mobile uses bottom sheets, web and admin use dialogs, and teal is the only action colour. Crimson never appears on the letter, the settlement block, the refund section, the trust tiles or any button. Amounts, units and numbers are in mono with tabular-nums. No en or em dashes in app copy or seeded template text; say "move", never "swap", never "slot" in app copy, and never call the prepaid amount an estimate or a deposit. Follow the spelling of "prepayment" that Phase 27 shipped.
- Demo triggers go in the Phase 14 registry only, never on the Control Panel page. The bar gets "Stage longer prepaid procedure" on Admin Review and "Pay out trust refund" on the Xero sim. The PWA gets the office stand-ins "Office sends a prepayment reminder" and "Office refunds this prepayment from the trust account" on the mobile Booking (badged office stand-in, as OFFICE_SIMULATION_ACTOR); the anaesthetist's own by-hand invoice and credit reuse 38b's and 39's review stand-ins. The letter picker, reminder, settlement actions, move lines, refund, payout, rebook and template actions are product UI, unbadged. Bodies live in src/shared or src/store so pwaPurity passes.
- Do not commit or push.

Phase goal: the prepayment story is finished: standard letters that state the prepaid amount as the price, picked at Approve and send, and reminders; after a prepaid procedure nothing invoiced or credited automatically, with the prepaid amount as the price, the recorded BTM for reference, and an additional invoice or a credit note (in full or, provisionally, for part of the prepayment) raised by hand by the anaesthetist or the office; prepayment money held in a trust account until the procedure and then released to whoever did it; a full refund from the trust account when a prepaid Booking is cancelled; when a prepaid Booking moves to another anaesthetist, by List or single Booking, an honour system with the agreed amount kept, nothing recalculated and, provisionally, only the payable's payee repointed; and a fresh prepayment at the replacement anaesthetist's own fixed price after a true cancellation and rebooking.

No default RVG Contract, hospital or insurer default, or second No contract (RVG) is ever created; No contract (RVG) is never loaded. No NZSA guide range check and no warning on loaded figures. - Modifiers: AA's own rows load from a sheet and become editable and retirable; the RVG table is 19b's, generated from AR-34's files, as printed, never re-transcribed and never edited.

Its units are never read, junk such as "10% discount" is excluded and cannot be approved, only AA-approved names load (and their lines with them), and loaded values come from the controlled spreadsheets. No Solutions Plus identifier is carried (US-13.4.3).
- Masters referenced by identity (hospitals, surgeons, rooms, groups, insurers, organisations and AA modifiers) retire, never delete. No contract (RVG) is never retired.
- Insurers (US-11.4.1): add, rename, retire and reinstate, with the direct-claims flag creating no Contract and no holder; "Set up as a contract holder" opens 18's holder panel prefilled. Scale and privacy

NFR After phases 34, 36, 37, 42 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 2 items covered

Scale: a "Load full-scale data" demo action (on Admin Day and Invoices, with a confirm) builds the whole practice in memory from the seed. That is 85 anaesthetists (the 14 demo anaesthetists unchanged plus 71 generated), Slots across Phase 28's horizon (about 21,000 at four months, shown as "sessions") and about 28,000 invoices over 12 months. The data is in the 2026-10-08 shapes: recurring bookings, ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED and DRAFT Lists, curated procedures in RVG groups, source wording, modifier records, a payer on every Booking, and exactly one Contract per Procedure by Phase 20's rule (No contract (RVG) or a Contract whose holder fits the Booking, never a default). It is built only through the one billing module in domain/billing: snapshot at authorise, invoices, BCTIs, ledger pairs, the weekly cycle and the monthly AA-FEE invoices. The 71 get no prepaid set. Saving pauses. A banner shows timings. Admin Day, Invoices, Audit, the Ledger and the Billing monitor page and filter at scale. Reset or reload returns to the seed. Privacy: an office-only raw-row view on Matching (reason required, audited, masked), with a harness entry showing another role refused; redacted diagnostics; a "Scan for NHI leaks" on the Data Inspector that also checks Xero for personal information (OQ-30); and a neutral "Synthetic data only" badge.

    The catalogue's pricing model end to end: surgeons' rooms and profiles with private not-preferred and preferred pairings and priority tiers guiding the office's pickers; contract holders (third and first party) and dated Contract versions with AA codes, and one No contract (RVG) with no hospital or insurer defaults; RVG groups under body sections, a curated procedure list with a general procedure per group and a two-tab picker; Contract lines with a fixed price, rate, discount or units, the anaesthetists' own price lists, and starting units from the line, procedure or group, any value accepted with an office warning when out of range; optional itemised modifiers, each explained when claimed, with age and the included P1 locked; one Contract per Procedure, mandatory at setup, No contract (RVG) first, and the three-part stack (source wording, procedure and RVG code, Contract) on every booking screen; the payer on the Booking, who is billed decided by the Contract's holder, the insurance indication and child-payer warnings and holder references; invoices sent by the run and a Split button with typed $ or % shares; the 3/2/2 modifier split, combination Contracts, one price precedence with fixed rate and discount and the anaesthetist adjustment on No contract (RVG) and their own Contracts only; and a lock at AUTHORISED that reproduces invoices exactly. S1 Beat 3, S2 Beat 2, S3, S4 Beat 3 and S5 are re-scripted.
  • After phase 27
    Prepayment from the anaesthetist's prepaid set of procedures and RVG groups for a person paying: the amount is their own fixed price from their first-party Contract, in full and shown to them, a missing price warns the office, the invoice is generated at setup with its ledger pair and draft Xero pair and sent on admin approval, part-paid tracking, a warning in both apps that strengthens as the date nears, and a prepaid Procedure billed at the prepaid amount with nothing raised automatically. S4 Beat 1 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 32a
    The office's schedule: every session stored and free by default over a configurable horizon, Slots and Lists, statuses as a user-maintained list, the availability calendar with series, the conflict dashboard, recurring bookings, Draft Lists in the DRAFT state that hold Bookings with a waiting flag (including from a recurring clash) and become ACTIVE when the office assigns them with preferences and tiers, anaesthetists returning or handing on their own Lists with no preference warning (also when they mark a booked session unavailable) and moving single Bookings, and the office's shared notification pool. S2 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 35
    S1 rebuilt: hospital sync, then the matching screen showing each row's wording as received, then a Booking whose Contract the office sets (No contract (RVG) first). Explicit save with change sets, and the on-demand update email picked from the change history, started from a template, to the rooms or the hospital, including from a List-move notification; nothing sent automatically.
  • After phase 39a
    The money story on the internal ledger: balances shown in or out of balance, Xero mirror resilience and a processing monitor grouped by anaesthetist with sorting and filters, ledger-backed web accounts with a flat outstanding list and a cash-basis GST schedule, the anaesthetist's main view from today with an archive and search for invoiced work, events on a Procedure with the events list and free-form additional invoices to any party (office and anaesthetist), the credit note option, credit-and-rebill from copied lines and a split combined procedure that equals the credit, and weekly ISO-week payment runs with BCTI approval, netting and a remittance advice.
